prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System:Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell;Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport retain authority. Aliases:Airline Operations Coordinator=Saffron;Regional Flow Manager=Copperfin;Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone;Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard;Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove;Tower Supervisor=Brindle(drills);Ramp Control Lead=Quartzline(voice/chat);Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor(training);Slot Coordinator=Halcyon(voice conferences);Tower Sequence Manager=Ironleaf(tower discussions). Airline Operations Centre→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange:Flight Intent Message;Identity Access Service authenticates;invalid/incomplete rejected(reason-codes);material intents supersede schedules;changes require messages. Business Rules Registry governs carrier/fairness rules. Marlinstone+Capacity Assessment Module→Blueharbor:demand/intents/Airport Capacity Plan/Airport Acceptance Rate/runway-metering/sector-loading;Marlinstone flags Target Off Block Time imbalance. Blueharbor→Adapter/Foxglove:Calculated Takeoff Time/Target Off Block Time/arrival-opportunities;Calculated Takeoff Time combines runway-metering/departure-fix-loading/Ground Delay Program rules. Capacity precedes preferences;priority:safety/emergency/humanitarian/national-obligation>scheduled-commercial>discretionary;fairness mandatory. Copperfin authorizes Capacity Reduction State exceptions/recovery/divergence;Halcyon confirms publication,requests network-delay/fairness adjustments. Orchard validates weather/provenance/overrides;Storm Cell Snapshot confidence/degradation/provisional-capacity visible;Meteorology Briefing Officer interprets. East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor→Ramp Movement Board→Surface Surveillance Adapter→Foxglove:advisory movements;Board timestamps stand-readiness/boarding-completion/doors-closed/start-approval-readiness/taxi-start/configured-events. Quartzline reconciles,constraint-checks apron/stands/restrictions,sends Stand Tow Request Form;Blueharbor recalculates. Tower Supervisor/Airport Duty Manager resolve conflicts;Runway Inspection Note precedes capacity endorsement;North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter receive capacities;Alert Distribution Hub distributes approvals. Saffron checks readiness/crew/connections/recovery;shall confirm operator-requested revisions in Foxglove before freeze-horizon;Ground Handling Dispatcher supplies milestone

New part:
S284: The Airline Operations Coordinator may request a sequence review when a flight has a valid operational reason to protect a connection, crew limit, or network rotation.
S285: The Slot Coordinator verifies that any proposed resequencing remains compatible with the Calculated Takeoff Time tolerance and the current Slot Compliance State.
S286: The Regional Flow Manager is notified when local resequencing threatens to erode the planned departure rate in the Airport Capacity Plan.
S287: Runway queue management favors stable ordering, but the Tower Supervisor may intervene when wake spacing, route restrictions, runway crossings, or emergency traffic require a change.
S288: Each manual sequence change is recorded in the Collaborative Decision Log with the user identity, timestamp, affected flight, and reason code.
S289: The Audit Event Ledger preserves the sequence history so that post-event review can distinguish operational necessity from avoidable volatility.
S290: Departure readiness checks combine aircraft operator status, ground handling status, cockpit readiness, route clearance availability, and surface position into a single tower-readable indicator.
S291: The Aircraft Operator Representative is responsible for keeping aircraft readiness information current enough for the tower team to trust the displayed status.
S292: The Ground Handling Dispatcher updates boarding, loading, door closure, and tow readiness milestones through the operational interface before the flight is considered eligible for pushback planning.
S293: Foxglove shall publish tower readiness changes to authenticated airline and handling users within the configured refresh interval.
S294: The Deicing Coordinator sends the Deicing Pad Queue Card when pad demand, treatment progress, or release timing changes.
S295: The deicing interface point exposes whether a flight still requires treatment, is waiting for pad access, is under treatment, or has been released for taxi within the protected time assumption.
S296: When deicing demand increases, the Tower Supervisor compares pad release expectations with runway queue gaps before accepting an aircraft into the active departure stream.
S297: During Adverse Weather Mode or a Capacity Reduction State, the Tower Sequence Manager applies the active spacing rules from the Business Rules Registry and highlights flights that may miss their Calculated Takeoff Time.
S298: In the Recovery Phase, the tower sequence workflow emphasizes measured acceleration rather than first-come recovery, because uncontrolled pushback surges can overload taxiways and recreate delay.
S299: Ground handling capacity is treated as a hard operational constraint because an aircraft cannot meet a feasible off-block time unless the required people, vehicles, and stand equipment are available at the stand before boarding closure.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
